item.title: Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has a slight illness. He thinks: 'Now this slight illness has arisen in me; there is reason to lie down. Let…
item.description:
Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has a slight illness. He thinks: 'Now this slight illness has arisen in me; there is reason to lie down. Let me lie down.' He lies down, not making an effort... unrealized. Bhikkhus, this is the seventh ground for laziness.
Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has just recovered from an illness, not long recovered. He thinks: 'I have just recovered from an illness, not long recovered. My body is weak due to illness and cannot bear it. Let me lie down.' He lies down, not making an effort... unrealized. Bhikkhus, this is the eighth ground for laziness.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 8.80

item.title: Elder Nhātakamuni: Afflicted by a wind disease, you live in the deep forest, With limited alms-gathering, lean and weak. What will a bhikkhu do with…
item.description:
Elder Nhātakamuni:

Afflicted by a wind disease, you live in the deep forest,
With limited alms-gathering, lean and weak.
What will a bhikkhu do with such a body?

My body is flooded with spreading joy and bliss.
Even though lean, I will live in the forest.

Developing the seven factors of enlightenment,
The five faculties and the five powers,
Possessing subtle jhāna, I live without taints.

Freed from the fetters, mind pure, unstained,
Always, well contemplating, I live without taints.

All taints, internal and external, that were previously in me —
All are cut off, they will not arise again.

The five aggregates are fully understood,
They stand with roots cut off.
The end of suffering is attained; now there is no more renewed existence.

From: Theragāthā 6.11

item.title: - Venerable Sāriputta, what is happiness and what is suffering? - Venerable sir, birth is suffering, non-birth is happiness. When there is birth, venerable sir,…
item.description:
- Venerable Sāriputta, what is happiness and what is suffering?
- Venerable sir, birth is suffering, non-birth is happiness. When there is birth, venerable sir, this suffering is to be expected: cold, heat, hunger, thirst, defecation, urination, contact with fire, contact with rod, contact with sword. Even relatives and friends, when they meet and gather, cause distress. Venerable sir, birth is suffering; when there is birth, this suffering is to be expected. When there is no birth, venerable sir, this happiness is to be expected: no cold, no heat, no hunger, no thirst, no defecation, no urination, no contact with fire, no contact with rod, no contact with sword. Even relatives and friends, when they meet and gather, cause no distress. Venerable sir, when there is no birth, this happiness is to be expected.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.65

item.title: Elder Subhūta: Placing oneself in a place not considered suitable, A person who wants to do a task but does not succeed — That task…
item.description:
Elder Subhūta:

Placing oneself in a place not considered suitable,
A person who wants to do a task but does not succeed —
That task is considered a failure.

If one abandons the winning stake, the root of suffering is drawn out.
It is like a gambler who, with bad luck, throws away the die.
If he throws away everything, he is no different from a blind man,
Not seeing the path, level or uneven.

Speak only of what you do, not of what you don't.
The wise know the one who only speaks but does not act.

Like a beautiful flower, colorful but without fragrance,
So well-spoken words are fruitful when acted upon.

Like a beautiful flower, colorful but also fragrant,
So well-spoken words are fruitless if not acted upon.

From: Theragāthā 5.2

item.title: Once, the Venerable Anuruddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Andhavana forest, afflicted with a severe illness, suffering, gravely ill. Then many bhikkhus went to…
item.description:
Once, the Venerable Anuruddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Andhavana forest, afflicted with a severe illness, suffering, gravely ill. Then many bhikkhus went to the Venerable Anuruddha and said to him: 'What abiding does the Venerable Anuruddha abide in, so that arisen painful bodily feelings do not affect his mind?' - 'Friends, because my mind is well established in the four foundations of mindfulness, arisen painful bodily feelings do not affect my mind. What four? Here, friends, I dwell contemplating the body as a body ... feelings as feelings ... mind as mind ... phenomena as phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. Friends, because my mind is well established in these four foundations of mindfulness, arisen painful bodily feelings do not affect my mind.'

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 52.10

item.title: So too, bhikkhus, for one who walks in what is not his own domain, in another's territory. Therefore, bhikkhus, do not walk in what is…
item.description:
So too, bhikkhus, for one who walks in what is not his own domain, in another's territory. Therefore, bhikkhus, do not walk in what is not your own domain, in another's territory. Bhikkhus, walking in what is not your own domain, in another's territory, Māra gains an opportunity, Māra gains an object. And what, bhikkhus, is not a bhikkhu's own domain, what is another's territory? It is the five strands of sensual pleasure. What five? There are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual desire, enticing. There are sounds cognizable by the ear ... odors cognizable by the nose ... tastes cognizable by the tongue ... tangibles cognizable by the body that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual desire, enticing. Bhikkhus, this is not a bhikkhu's own domain, this is another's territory. Bhikkhus, walk in your own domain, in the territory of your parents. Bhikkhus, walking in your own domain, in the territory of your parents, Māra does not gain an opportunity, Māra does not gain an object. And what, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu's own domain, what is the territory of his parents? It is the four foundations of mindfulness. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body as a body ... feelings as feelings ... mind as mind ... phenomena as phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. This, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu's own domain, the territory of his parents.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 47.6

item.title: Elder Ramaṇīyavihāri: Like a good thoroughbred, well-trained, of good breed, Having stumbled, stands up again, steady. I possess right view, a disciple of the Perfectly…
item.description:
Elder Ramaṇīyavihāri:

Like a good thoroughbred, well-trained, of good breed,
Having stumbled, stands up again, steady.
I possess right view, a disciple of the Perfectly Enlightened One.

From: Theragāthā 1.45

item.title: Both in the past and now, Sajjha, I have said: 'A bhikkhu who is an Arahant, with taints destroyed, accomplished, done what had to be…
item.description:
Both in the past and now, Sajjha, I have said: 'A bhikkhu who is an Arahant, with taints destroyed, accomplished, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, attained the goal, destroyed the fetter of existence, rightly liberated — he cannot transgress nine things: A bhikkhu with taints destroyed cannot intentionally deprive a living being of life; a bhikkhu with taints destroyed cannot take what is not given, that is, stealing; a bhikkhu with taints destroyed cannot engage in sexual intercourse; a bhikkhu with taints destroyed cannot knowingly speak falsely; a bhikkhu with taints destroyed cannot enjoy sensual pleasures from stored-up goods as he did when he was a householder. A bhikkhu with taints destroyed cannot reject the Buddha; a bhikkhu with taints destroyed cannot reject the Dhamma; a bhikkhu with taints destroyed cannot reject the Saṅgha; a bhikkhu with taints destroyed cannot reject the training.'

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.8

item.title: Bhikkhus, this is my instruction to you. All conditioned things are impermanent. Strive on with diligence for your own liberation. Before long, the Tathāgata will…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, this is my instruction to you. All conditioned things are impermanent. Strive on with diligence for your own liberation. Before long, the Tathāgata will attain final Nibbāna. Three months from today, the Tathāgata will attain final Nibbāna.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 16 – Mahāparinibbānasutta

item.title: Poṭṭhapāda, I teach the Dhamma for the abandonment of the gross self-identification. If you practice accordingly, then defiled states will be abandoned, pure states will…
item.description:
Poṭṭhapāda, I teach the Dhamma for the abandonment of the gross self-identification. If you practice accordingly, then defiled states will be abandoned, pure states will increase, and you will personally realize, attain, and abide in the here and now with full and extensive wisdom. Poṭṭhapāda, it is possible that you might think: 'Defiled states will be abandoned, pure states will increase, and one will personally realize, attain, and abide in the here and now with full and extensive wisdom, yet suffering still remains.' Poṭṭhapāda, do not think thus. When defiled states are abandoned and pure states increase, one in this very life, with direct knowledge, attains and abides in full and extensive wisdom, then joy arises, gladness, tranquility, mindfulness, clear comprehension, and a pleasant abiding arise.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 9 – Poṭṭhapādasutta
